text: Astronomy examines celestial bodies, space, and the universe in its entirety. A core principle is the orbit, defined as the trajectory an object traces around a more massive body under gravitational influence. Planets, asteroids, comets, stars, and galaxies all move along such paths. Knowledge of these orbits allows scientists to forecast events including planetary alignments, eclipses, and supernovae. Craters found on the moon, Mars, and other worlds result from frequent asteroid and comet collisions, illustrating an active cosmic environment.
